# Fixed: A queued rescan no longer fails when one of its artists was deleted

Part of the [custom Lidarr image](https://github.com/chodeus/Lidarr/tree/custom) (`ghcr.io/chodeus/lidarr:custom`), which merges this branch into `develop`. Reviewed in [#58](https://github.com/chodeus/Lidarr/pull/58).

A rescan command names the artists it is for by id. `DiskScanService.Scan` read them back with `GetArtists`, which throws when an id is no longer stored, and also when one is repeated, and it did so after walking its folders. Commands wait in a queue, and a delete through the API or the UI doesn't, so an artist deleted before or during the scan failed it for every artist on it. By then the scan had already cleaned the database rows of files missing from its folders, so nothing was imported or matched in that run.

- The scan reads its artists once, before any folder is cleaned, in one query that returns only the artists still stored, once each (`IArtistService.GetStoredArtists`, backed by `IArtistRepository.FindStored`; both have default bodies that behave like `GetArtists`, so other implementations keep compiling). A scan with no artist ids is unchanged.
- The artists are used to report skipped artists, to check for missing artist folders, and to publish an `ArtistScannedEvent` for each when the scan completes. One deleted while the scan runs is still on that list, so it may be reported or its folder checked, but the scan reads the stored artists again before it creates missing artist folders and before the completion events, and uses those records: it creates no folder for an artist deleted meanwhile, and the events, whose handlers write extra and metadata files into the artist's folder, leave such an artist out and carry the current path of one that moved. The scan doesn't fail.

Tests: `ScanDeletedArtistFixture` runs the scan against the real `ArtistService` and repository over the test database; the disk, import decisions and media files are mocked. A scan naming a deleted artist still checks the stored artist's folder and makes its import decisions, as does one whose artist is deleted while it reads the folders; a missing root folder reports only the stored artist as skipped, and an artist named twice is checked once; an artist deleted while the folders are read gets no completion event and no recreated folder, while the others do; and an artist moved meanwhile is reported at its new path. All but the moved-artist test fail on `develop`; that one passes there because `develop` read the artists after walking the folders, and here it guards the second read. The mid-scan test also fails with the ids filtered only at the start. Leaving out the stored-artist query, or either second read, fails a test. The two `UpgradeMediaFileServiceFixture` tests that fail in a Debug build on a stray warning fail on `develop` too.
